PLAN "3-Week Reconditioning Block: Return-to-Baseline"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Return to baseline strength after illness"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 45m "Reconditioning Upper/Lower Hybrid":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          squat 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
          bent_over_row 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 3 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 40m "Lower Focus Endurance":
        warmup:
          jogging_in_place 3 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x8..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          leg_extension 3x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          hip_thrust 3x8..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_flexor_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Friday training 45m "Upper Press & Pull Light":
        warmup:
          rowing 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          incline_press 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 2 minutes
  WEEK 2:
    DAY Monday training 50m "Volume Reintroduction":
      warmup:
        cycling 5 minutes
      main straight_sets:
        bench_press 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        squat 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
        barbell_row 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
      cooldown:
        total_body_light_stretch 3 minutes
    DAY Wednesday training 45m "Tempo & Mobility":
      warmup:
        brisk_walk 4 minutes
      main straight_sets:
        incline_press 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        deadlift 3x5..6 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
        cable_row 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
      cooldown:
        thoracic_spine_mobility 3 minutes
    DAY Friday training 50m "Pull+Core Focus":
      warmup:
        jumping_jack 2 minutes
      main straight_sets:
        dumbbell_row 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        lat_pulldown 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        pull_up 3x4..6 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
      cooldown:
        hollow_hold 2 minutes
  WEEK 3:
    DAY Monday training 55m "Return-to-Progression Prep":
      warmup:
        jog_in_place 5 minutes
      main straight_sets:
        bench_press 3x5..7 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        squat 3x5..7 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
        barbell_row 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
      cooldown:
        full_body_light_mobility 4 minutes
    DAY Wednesday training 50m "Conditioning & Technique":
      warmup:
        row 5 minutes
      main straight_sets:
        incline_press 3x5..7 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        deadlift 3x4..6 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
        cable_row 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
      cooldown:
        lat_stretch 2 minutes
    DAY Friday training 50m "Voluntary Push-Pull & Mobility":
      warmup:
        cycling 4 minutes
      main straight_sets:
        dumbbell_press 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        shrug 3x8..12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        face_pull 3x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
      cooldown:
        shoulder_metween_stretch 2 minutes

SYNTAX RULES:
- Rep ranges use TWO dots, not a dash. Correct: 3x8..12 rpe 7
- Sets always come first: 3x10 means 3 sets of 10 reps
- RPE goes after sets/reps: rpe 7
- Rest in seconds: rest 90 seconds

PLAN "Nutrition targets for 3-Week Reconditioning Block"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary nutrition:
    name "Estimate target caloric intake and macronutrient targets to support reconditioning and weight regain"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 0m "Nutrition Guidance":
        main:
          - target_calories 2600
          - protein_grams 170
          - carbs_grams 300
          - fats_grams 70
        notes:
          - baseline estimate based on weight loss and recent illness; adjust by 200 kcal/day depending on progress
          - protein ~1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight to preserve lean mass
          - distribute protein across 3–4 meals, include protein post-workout
          - prioritize nutrient-dense carbohydrates around training sessions
          - stay hydrated; monitor sodium if sweating increases
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Monday training 0m "Nutrition Guidance":
        main:
          - target_calories 2700
          - protein_grams 170
          - carbs_grams 320
          - fats_grams 75
        notes:
          - reassess weekly weight and appetite; add ~100–200 kcal if weight not increasing
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Monday training 0m "Nutrition Guidance":
        main:
          - target_calories 2800
          - protein_grams 175
          - carbs_grams 340
          - fats_grams 75
        notes:
          - aim to regain pre-illness weight while maintaining training progression

SYNTAX RULES:
- Provide calories and macros as plain values
- Units: calories, grams
- Emphasize protein range and per-meal distribution
- Include brief notes for adjustments based on weekly monitoring

ADDITIONAL NOTES:
- Estimate pre-illness maintenance calories roughly around 2900–3100 kcal for a 41-year-old male intermediate lifter; using conservative reconditioning targets initially (2600–2800 kcal) to support gradual weight regain without excessive fat gain
- If weight loss continues beyond 0.5–1.0 kg/week, increment calories by 200–300 kcal per week
- Consider fiber intake 25–35 g/day; include micronutrient-dense foods
- Monitor symptoms: fatigue, sleep quality, digestion; adjust carbohydrate around training to support energy
- Example meal timing near workouts:
  - Pre-workout: 30–60 g carbs, moderate protein
  - Post-workout: 20–40 g protein, 40–60 g carbs

PLAN "Reconditioning Block: Week 1 Load Continuation Assessment"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Assess feasibility of starting at pre-illness loads vs Week 1 light work"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 45m "Assessment: Start at Pre-illness Loads?":
        notes:
          - Client reports normal energy and readiness.
          - Question: can we start Week 1 with pre-illness loads (bench 100, squat 140, deadlift 170) or should we still revert to light reconditioning?
        guidance:
          - Risk assessment:
            - Illness-related fatigue can linger; back-to-baseline loads may increase risk of re-injury or excessive soreness.
            - 3 weeks off is moderate; tissue adaptation time varies; pre-illness loads assume full recovery and conditioning.
          - Suggested approach (gradual ramp rather than full load):
            - Option A (conservative): Start Week 1 with reduced load (about 80–85% of pre-illness top work sets) for 3–4 weeks, monitor RPE and recovery.
            - Option B (moderate): Start Week 1 with pre-illness loads for compound lifts but with reduced reps (e.g., 3x5–6 at 70–75% 1RM) and higher technique focus, then progress in Week 2 if tolerance is good.
            - Option C (full-start) only if objective measures show full restoration of appetite, sleep, and no lingering symptoms, plus ability to perform controlled reps with RPE around 6–7 and minimal fatigue the next day.
          - Practical plan if choosing Option A (conservative ramp):
            main sets:
              bench_press 3x5..6 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
              squat 3x5..6 rpe 6 rest 150 seconds
              deadlift 3x5..6 rpe 6 rest 150 seconds
            cardio: optional light, 10–15 minutes easy
            notes:
              - re-evaluate after Week 1; if tolerance is excellent, consider bumped loads to 90–95% of pre-illness over Week 2.
          - Practical plan if choosing Option B (moderate):
            main sets:
              bench_press 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
              squat 3x6..8 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
              deadlift 3x5..7 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
            notes:
              - maintain technique, watch signs of excessive fatigue.
          - Practical plan if choosing Option C (full-start):
            main sets:
              bench_press 3x3..5 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
              squat 3x3..5 rpe 6 rest 150 seconds
              deadlift 3x3..5 rpe 6 rest 150 seconds
            notes:
              - only if high-quality reps and no adverse symptoms; plan to gauge progression weekly.
        cooldown:
          mobility and light stretch: 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 0m "Assessment Note Only":
        main:
          - evaluation of subjective energy, sleep, appetite
          - plan adjustment based on Week 1 response
      DAY Friday training 0m "Decision Point":
        main:
          - finalize starting approach for Week 1 or transition to Week 2 style if tolerance is confirmed

SYNTAX RULES:
- Rep ranges use TWO dots, not a dash. Correct: 3x6..8 rpe 6
- Sets always come first: 3x5..6 means 3 sets of 5–6 reps
- RPE goes after sets/reps: rpe 6
- Rest in seconds: rest 90 seconds

PLAN " readiness signals for returning to full intensity work"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Identify objective and subjective readiness markers for progression to full-intensity training"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 0m "Readiness Signals Overview":
        main:
          - topic "Readiness criteria"
          - points:
              - subjective_energy: "Consistent energy levels comparable to baseline on most days"
              - sleep_quality: "7–9 hours with minimal disturbances on most nights"
              - appetite_trends: "Stable or returning to baseline appetite"
              - training_fatigue_next_day: "No excessive soreness or fatigue (>4/10) the day after sessions"
              - symptom_check: "No fever, persistent cough, or flu-like symptoms; no GI issues"
              - performance_stability: "Ability to maintain prescribed RPEs within target range for 2–3 consecutive sessions"
              - injury_pain: "No new or worsening joint/muscle pain during or after sessions"
              - HRV_or_resting_hr: "Resting heart rate within 2–3 bpm of baseline or trending down if previously elevated"
              - movement_quality: "No compensatory mechanics; technique stays solid under load"
        notes:
          - Use a simple readiness log after each session
          - If 3 of 5 core criteria are clearly positive for 2 consecutive sessions, consider credentialing progression
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Wednesday training 0m "Objective Readiness Checks":
        main:
          - metric_pa: "Rate of perceived exertion (RPE) accuracy compared to plan; aim within 0–1 spread"
          - metric_perf: "First two working sets show ≤1 repetition impulse drop vs Week prior; no abrupt drop in total reps"
          - metric_recovery: "≥24 hours between intense sessions with no lingering fatigue"
        decision_rules:
          - ready_for_full_intensity: "If criteria met across subjective + objective markers for two consecutive training days"
          - hold_and_reassess: "If variables are mixed; extend Week 2 with gradual intensification plan"
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Friday training 0m "Formal Progression Decision":
        main:
          - plan:
              - ready: "Yes = proceed to full-intensity program in next block"
              - caution: "No = continue gradual ramp with elevated monitoring; revert to lighter loads if needed"
        notes:
          - Document rationale and thresholds used
          - Ensure medical clearance if any unresolved symptoms or aberrant markers

SIGNAL CATEGORIES:
  - subjective_signals:
      energy, sleep, appetite, overall mood, perceived recovery
  - objective_signals:
      resting_heart_rate, HRV (if tracked), sleep duration, training volume tolerance (RPE alignment, reps completed vs planned), movement quality, injury/pain status
  - performance_signals:
      consistency of technique, ability to hit target reps/sets with expected RPE, speed of bar, bar path quality
  - recovery_signals:
      24–48h recovery between sessions, absence of persistent soreness, ability to perform next session with similar effort

DECISION FRAMEWORK:
  - If 4+ objective/subjective signals trending positive and no pain/injury, proceed to planned full-intensity block with documented monitoring
  - If mixed signals or 1–2 negative indicators, implement a staged ramp with smaller load increases and continue monitoring
  - If any red flags (fever, prolonged fatigue, significant sleep disruption, new injury), pause progression and re-evaluate with clinician

MONITORING TOOLS:
  - daily fatigue and energy log
  - sleep duration/quality notes
  - training RPE vs prescribed RPE comparison
  - post-workout soreness scale (0–10)
  - resting heart rate first thing in morning
  - simple movement screen tests as needed (e.g., hip hinge, squat depth, shoulder phenotype) to detect technique degradation
